title: Inflammation-type dysbiosis of the oral microbiome associates with COVID-19 symptom duration and long COVID
summary: In a prospective cohort, Boruta-selected random-forest models with 5-fold cross-validation associated oral microbiome features with symptom duration among 27 followed patients. For long COVID, the best species-plus-clinical model had F1 0.615 and the pathway-only model had F1 0.689. This small observational analysis supports association, not causation or prospective clinical utility; the journal page gives first publication as 17 August 2021 and issue date as 22 October 2021.
ai_technology: Random-forest classification with Boruta feature selection and 5-fold cross-validation

evidence.tested: Of 84 PCR-positive patients, 27 completed 4- and 10-week follow-up. Boruta feature selection and random-forest classification with 5-fold cross-validation gave F1 0.615 for a clinical-data-plus-microbiome-species long-COVID model and 0.689 for a pathway-only model; models without microbiome inputs showed no long-COVID signal.
evidence.unknown: The small cohort does not establish causality, external replication, or performance of a frozen model in prospective clinical use.
evidence.ai_role: Random-forest classifiers use oral microbiome and clinical features to estimate symptom-duration outcomes; Boruta selects features before 5-fold cross-validation.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
